units.text: INT. LIGHTSHIP TELEGRAPH CABIN - NIGHT (1894)
A cramped wooden cabin that rolls with each swell.
A brass lamp swings on a chain.
Charts on the wall.
A wireless set, new and awkward, squats on a table beside a tin cup of cold tea.
A WOMAN, 30s, sits very upright in a wool coat buttoned to the chin, a clerk's cap pinned over her hair.
Her hands rest in her lap, folded as if for prayer.
A pencil sits behind her ear.
She has the calm of someone who has decided something.
She dips a pen and begins to write on a telegraph form.
The nib scratches.
The ship groans.
She writes without pause, as if the words have been waiting.
Dear Mother. The sea is quiet tonight. I have eaten, and I have slept, and the keeper tells me the fog will lift by morning. You mustn't worry that I have not written. There was nothing to say.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She stops.
Reads the line back, soundless.
Crosses out "nothing" and writes "little."
She sets the pen down.
It is not true that I am happy. But I am not unhappy. I am in the place where one is neither, which I have come to prefer.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: A lazy swell lifts the cabin and lets it down.
She does not stir.
She picks up the cup, tastes the tea, grimaces, and puts it back.
On the table, the wireless set clicks twice.
She watches it.
Nothing follows.
She takes up the pen once more.
By the time you read this, the inspector will have come, and he will have found the log in good order. I want you to know that I kept it so. Every entry, every hour.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She lifts the lamp from its hook and sets it on the table.
The wick flares.
In its light we see that the corner of the log book is charred, a black fan of ash across three pages.
She turns the log to face her and closes it with a decisive thump.
The wireless set clicks again, three long, one short.
She stiffens.
Her pencil comes down from her ear and begins to write the code as it arrives, in neat block capitals.
She reads it.
Reads it again.
Slowly, she tears the form from its pad.
She folds it in thirds.
She sets it inside her coat, against her heart.
Forgive me, Mother. I have done a thing, and I will not ask you to understand it. Only that when they ask you my name, you will say it plainly.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She reaches for the letter and signs it, in a firm hand, at the bottom.
INSERT - THE LETTER
The signature reads: ODILE MARCHAND.
BACK TO SCENE
ODILE sets down the pen and stands.
She puts on her cap, straightens the coat.
Takes the lamp.
The wireless clicks again, insistent.
Odile blows out the flame.
In the dark, the ship rolls on.
A door opens, a rush of wind, and the sound of the sea.
It is a quiet night.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: The door shuts.
